comparison_audit.backend: DREAMPlaceFPGA can emit Bookshelf placement and, for its limited Ultrascale+ flow, FPGA Interchange physical output/DCP conversion; it does not emit the clustered VPR .place contract used by the frozen matrix.
blockers: The current TilePlace matrix starts from already packed VPR clustered netlists, whereas DREAMPlaceFPGA starts from flat Bookshelf or FPGA Interchange logical netlists.
DREAMPlaceFPGA performs its own LUT/FF packing and legalization, so cluster identity and the packed netlist change.
Its supplied architectures target simplified Xilinx Ultrascale or a limited Ultrascale+ FPGA Interchange flow, not the VTR architectures used by the six frozen cases.
Using its native output would also change the final routing/backend methodology.
comparison_audit.defensible_future_use: Create a separately labeled Bookshelf or FPGA Interchange/Vivado cohort with frozen conversion, packing, and common-backend rules; do not merge it into the current six-case VPR table.
input_formats: FPGA Interchange .netlist and .device converted to Bookshelf
comparison_audit.placement_scope: flat global placement plus packing/legalization and optional detailed placement

status.promotion_to_B0: blocked until a methodologically defensible separate cohort is specified and a complete local run archives commands, logs, outputs, legality, QoR, and backend evidence

build_audit.reason_not_attempted: Building the sample VCU108 flow would create a separate Vivado primitive/device experiment and would not produce a comparable row in the frozen VPR matrix.

comparison_audit.backend: Generated placement Tcl is loaded into an implemented Vivado design; the script clears/replaces placement, invokes Vivado placement handling for remaining primitives, and routes with Vivado.
blockers: AMF-Placer consumes Xilinx primitive, device, macro, fixed-unit, clock, and timing data extracted from an already implemented Vivado design, not a VPR packed netlist.
The bundled device and benchmark flow targets VCU108/Ultrascale and uses Vivado site/BEL semantics rather than the current VTR architecture grid.
Its output is a Vivado placement Tcl/checkpoint flow and cannot be passed unchanged to the frozen VPR router.
The public repository is the basic implementation, documented as about 5% below the separately distributed advanced version.
comparison_audit.defensible_future_use: Run a separately labeled commercial-device/Vivado experiment with fixed design checkpoints, extraction hashes, Tcl replay, and the same Vivado routing methodology for every placer.
input_formats: Vivado-extracted zipped primitive netlist and cluster data
fixed-unit, macro, clock, and timing files referenced by JSON
comparison_audit.placement_scope: mixed-size primitive-level analytical placement, legalization, packing, and timing refinement

status.promotion_to_B0: blocked until a separate Vivado cohort is specified and a complete local run archives dependency licenses, extraction inputs, commands, logs, Tcl output, routed legality, QoR, and backend evidence

methodology_decision.current_six_case_matrix: Keep conventional VPR, VPR cluster-level AP, and TilePlace as the only same-packed-netlist/same-router rows.
methodology_decision.external_placer_claim: No independent external placer QoR result has been reproduced; neither candidate supports a direct superiority claim.
methodology_decision.next_preferred_direction: Expand the post-freeze VPR/Koios cohort under the existing frozen strategy before investing in a separate external-format flow.
methodology_decision.separate_experiment_option: A future FPGA Interchange/Vivado study must be pre-registered as a distinct cohort with its own netlist, architecture, packing, conversion, and backend controls.
